Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Eight players were handed qualifying offers by Monday, and that includes Seattle Mariners star Randy Arozarena . The outfielder received a $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Mariners, as reported by Bob Nightengale of USA Today. Of course, it is up to Arozarena whether to take that offer, but he also has an opportunity to look for a bigger bag in the MLB offseason. Arozarena has played the last three seasons with the Mariners, earning two All-Star nods along the way with the team. He is coming off his best season yet in the big leagues, slashing .281/.381/.484 and hitting 26 home runs to go along with 79 RBIs and 26 stolen bases across 154 games (670 plate appearances). Arozarena also posted a 148 OPS+. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Given the season he just had, the former American League Rookie of the Year Award winner Arozarena can expect other teams to show him the money in pursuit of his services. It is also worth noting that this is just the first time that the Mariners have extended a qualifying offer to a player in over a decade. Before Arozarena, it was pitcher Hisashi Iwakuma in who was the most recent player to receive such a gesture from Seattle. Apart from Arozarena, the other players who have already received qualifying offers from their respective 2026 teams are Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki, Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe, Baltimore Orioles starter Trevor Rogers, San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon and Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers.

item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Rumors swirled that Saquon Barkley might leave Philadelphia, but the running back shut them down with a clear message. After a tough loss to Washington, he told reporters he wants to fix the team’s problems, not run away from them. The Eagles lost their sixth straight game on Sunday night, falling 27-10 to the Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Trade talk often follows a bad streak, yet Barkley made his stance known immediately. He knows the season is going poorly, but he refuses to jump ship when things get hard. This loyalty matters for a fanbase that has seen too much change in recent years. A Clear Message to the Locker Room Barkley spoke plainly about his future after the game ended on Sunday night. According to the Associated Press, he told reporters, “I would love to be here.” He added that he does not want to be the type of player who leaves when the season turns sour. The team needs players who stick around to help find a solution. He is not the only one dealing with issues. Quarterback Jalen Hurts also faces injury concerns, and the roster is thin at several spots. Despite these hurdles, Barkley wants to be part of the answer. Heavy.com reported that he said, “I would love to be here. I plan on being here.” The Ravens acquired offensive lineman Cam Jurgens from General Manager Howie Roseman in exchange for draft picks. This move shows the front office is willing to make changes to improve the team’s future. Yet, Barkley insists he will stay to help the current group get back on track. Playing Through the Pain Barkley has not been at 100 percent for most of the season. He missed the first two days of practice this week due to a hamstring and back injury. NBC Sports Philadelphia noted that he returned on Friday to explain his mindset. He told the media, “One day, I’m not going to be playing football.” He said he does not want to look back and wonder if he could have tried harder. item.description: Valkyries players Cecilia Zandalasini, Kaila Charles and Kayla Thornton conduct their exit interviews at the Sephora Performance Center in Oakland, Calif. Chronicle) The Golden State Valkyries are still nursing sore muscles and lost voices from their title celebration on Halloween night. Many are still catching up to the hundreds of congratulatory text messages and calls pouring in. "I think everybody that I know in life hit me up," Kiah Stokes said on Monday morning. Gabby Williams , the Finals MVP for her heroic 28 second-half points in Game 7, woke up on Monday morning to a text from a fellow Finals MVP, one who won it six times over with the Chicago Bulls. "Michael Jordan texted me," Williams said, adding that she savors recognition from her colleagues and teammates more than any public adoration. "Having so many past teammates just genuinely who followed my trajectory reached out to me, that meant a lot to me." The Valkyries prevailed over the WNBA's first seven-game series in history, and now the championship tour has begun. The team kicked the tour off on Sunday back at the arena where they made history - just 24 hours after toppling the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 - to show off the trophy and celebrate with fans at the Warriors ' game against the Los Angeles Clippers (the NBA team with which Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase got her start as an assistant). Players sat courtside to watch the Warriors rout the Clippers while Veronica Burton relived the title run with Warriors broadcasters Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike for the telecast. On Monday, the entire team gathered for exit interviews with the media - the opulent silver championship trophy next to them while they fielded questions. One player absent was the WNBA's unanimous sixth player of the yea r honoree, Janelle Salaün , who wasn't there because of a prior commitment, the team said. It was a strange postseason for Salaün. She epitomized the depth the Valkyries prided themselves on by setting scoring records from players off the bench, but she saw her role minimized in the playoffs, including her being benched in the final three games of the Finals. Rookie Juste Jocyte , the fifth overall pick of the 2025 draft, wasn't much of a participant during the regular season after her late arrival and was relegated to garbage time minutes in the playoffs. She said on Monday she came to terms with the lack of playing time. "I also feel like just putting everything aside and wanting the best for your team," she said. item.title: Houston Astros exercise club option on Isaac Paredes' contract for 2027 season
item.description: Picking up Isaac Paredes' option could save the Astros money as he was projected to earn more in arbitration had the sides gone that route. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) The Houston Astros exercised a $13.35 million club option on infielder Isaac Paredes for 2027, the team announced Monday, an anticipated move after his productive 2026 season. Paredes was under team control regardless for 2027, his final year of salary arbitration eligibility. Had the Astros declined his option, Paredes would have gone through the arbitration process again this winter. MLB Trade Rumors projects Paredes would earn $15 million in arbitration, higher than the option figure, so picking up the option is a potential cost-saving move for Houston. Paredes, 27, posted an .806 OPS with 25 home runs and tied for sixth in the American League with 94 RBIs this season while playing 155 games. He served as the Astros' everyday third baseman for most of the season with Carlos Correa suffering a season-ending ankle injury in early May. Correa is expected to be back healthy in 2027. The resulting infield surplus - especially at the corners - raises the possibility the Astros could explore trade options with Paredes or shortstop Jeremy Peña this offseason. Paredes was also a subject of trade discussions last winter. The salary in his option marks a $4 million raise from Paredes' salary of $9.35 million in 2026. The club option still could become a mutual option if Paredes places top-10 in Most Valuable Player voting. The MVP results will be announced Nov. 12. item.title: Renato Moicano speaks out on Dan Miragliotta controversy
item.description: UFC Vegas 123 took place this weekend and delivered entertaining fights and consequential results. However, the biggest news of the weekend came in the main event, and it wasn’t the winner’s performance. In the main event, Tom Nolan defeated Renato Moicano via third-round TKO. The result carries a heavy amount of controversy, as Moicano was on track to enter the third round up two rounds to none, but didn’t because of a referee decision. MORE: Sean Brady injured, replaced in UFC Vegas 124 main-event slot In the second round, Moicano was on Nolan’s back and had a body triangle locked in. That’s one of the more dominant positions a fighter can have. With 1:12 seconds left in the second round, referee Dan Miragliotta breaks up the position and stands the fighters up. No joke I think this is top 5 worst ref standups of all time pic.twitter.com/Id02M2PWko — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 1, 2026 A referee isn’t supposed to stand fighters up unless there is literally no advancement and the fighter in the dominant position isn’t putting out any offense. Usually, stand-ups happen when a fighter has top control, or there’s a clinch against the fence with little action. A body triangle is a difficult position to get, and Moicano wasn’t just stalling once he had it. That position can be used to throw strikes or, especially, to find a submission. It was also clearly a point of emphasis in Moicano’s game plan. In the first round, Moicano took the same position, knowing Nolan couldn’t defend it. That’s not stalling a fight; that’s exploiting your opponent’s weaknesses. After the separation, Nolan hurt Moicano to end the round, and then finished him early in round three. Since the fight, Moicano has spoken about the controversial decision and isn’t shy about how he feels. Giving Nolan credit is still fair; Moicano was adamant that Nolan was the better striker on the night. That said, it’s still egregious; Moicano wouldn’t have been as hurt going into round three if Miragliotta had stayed out of the fight. item.title: Tyler Kolek’s Perfect Start Hits A Hard Wall
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Tyler Kolek’s perfect start to the season ended on Friday night with a reality check that no amount of hope can fix. The third-year guard, who had dished out 21 assists without a single turnover, coughed up the ball twice in just 13 minutes of play against the 76ers. This sudden drop in performance comes at a bad time for a player who has been the only bright spot in an otherwise struggling New York Knicks lineup. Since Jose Alvarado suffered a left ankle sprain, the Knicks have watched Kolek advance in the hierarchy. Daily Knicks reported that Alvarado has returned to practice and is now listed as “questionable” on the injury report. This shift means Kolek must now beat out the very player he replaced to keep his spot in the rotation. While averaging more than 14 minutes per game alongside Alvarado in the rotation, these stats offer no assurance of his future once veterans recover. The Turnover Streak Ends For the first two seasons, Kolek struggled with ball security more than almost anyone else in the league. With 17.3 percent of his possessions ending in turnovers, he posted the 14th-highest rate among 150 players logging comparable minutes. That stat line changed completely at the start of this year, as he posted 25 assists against just two turnovers. However, Yahoo Sports noted that this impressive streak of 21 assists without a turnover finally broke on Friday. In the game against Philadelphia, Kolek went just 1-for-3 from the field while committing two turnovers. The loss of that streak was a major blow to his case for more minutes. He was far from the only player with a bad night, as Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby, and Josh Hart all struggled in their own ways. Yet, the point guard’s inability to protect the ball when it mattered most reminded fans that the backup role is still up for grabs. A Fluid Backcourt Battle Until the team stabilizes, Head coach Mike Brown has stated he will remain committed to veteran players. Only when the early-season slump ends or another injury occurs will he give developmental players like Kolek more time. The situation is complicated because Alvarado offers a different skill set than Kolek. While Alvarado brings elite defense and energy, his shooting can be streaky, and he is not the same level of passer as the rookie. Kolek has shown he can make the Knicks offense run better. When he is on the court with Karl-Anthony Towns, the team scores 8.7 more points per 100 possessions. He also assisted on 53.2 percent of the team’s baskets when he played, the highest mark in the entire league among players with more than one appearance. These numbers show why the Knicks might need to keep him in the mix, even if his recent game was a step backward. item.title: Why Texas A&M coach Mike Elko is sticking with Marcel Reed at QB instead of giving Brady Hart a shot
item.description: Texas A&M reserve QB Brady Hart has been limited to mop-up time this season. (Joe Buvid/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Texas A&M coach Mike Elko provided some insight Monday into his coaching mindset for why backup quarterback Brady Hart hasn't been given an opportunity on Saturdays despite Marcel Reed 's struggles. "We feel like Brady gets a ton of opportunities to showcase where he's at, a ton of opportunities to show us whether or not he's ready to go or step in and be the guy," Elko said during his weekly news conference ahead of Saturday's game at South Carolina. "The challenge to him has been if you want opportunities, there's a level that we need to see in order to feel comfortable about doing that." Elko has continued to put his trust in Reed throughout the season, even if the senior quarterback's play has been well below the level he played at last season. Hart has gotten only garbage time reps throughout the season with only one pass attempt coming in SEC play, but Elko did consider going to Hart in the Alabama game. Hart warmed up on the sidelines after Reed threw his second interception within the first five minutes of the game. But Texas A&M elected to stay with Reed after the play, and he did respond with some of his best football of the season. Reed finished with 163 passing yards and the Aggies offense went 4-for-4 on red zone scoring opportunities. They even entered the fourth quarter with a lead before the Crimson Tide reached a higher gear to win 31-20 . "Through the second and third quarter of that game, I thought offensive efficiency was as good as it's been," Elko said. "We didn't finish the game obviously the way we would have wanted to, and didn't get it done in the fourth quarter the way we needed to to be successful. But I think some of the growth is there." On the whole, Reed has been among the least productive quarterbacks in the SEC. Reed is tied for the conference lead in interceptions. He is last among qualified quarterbacks in completion percentage (56.8%) and second-to-last in quarterback rating (114.4). Only Mississippi State backup quarterback Parker Puckett has a lower quarterback rating. Reed has thrown for over 200 yards just twice this season and only once in SEC play while totaling at least two touchdowns in a game just once since the season-turning loss to Kentucky in Week 3. But even amid it all Elko has said that Reed remains the guy, stating some version of the refrain that he gives the Aggies the best shot to win on gamedays. That will remain the case, it seems, going forward. "There's a lot that Marcel can improve on, for sure," Elko said during last week's SEC coaches teleconference, according to The Bryan-College Station Eagle. item.title: Dusty May Reveals Dallas’ Three-Point Defense Secret
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The biggest shift in Dallas’ defense isn’t a new scheme or a complex play. It is actually the referees letting players hit each other harder. Coach Dusty May said the league is allowing more physical contact on ball handlers in the open court, and the Mavericks are using that rule to their advantage. May told reporters that this change in how the game is officiated encourages his team to play more aggressively. The staff feels safe picking up opponents higher up the floor because the officials allow for more physicality without calling fouls. This creates a safer environment for defenders to take risks and force turnovers. “The point of attack defense and the physicality that you can use on an open court ball handler encourages you to pick up more because there’s very little risk,” May said, according to Yardbarker . While the team did give up two layups in a previous game due to these aggressive pickups, the strategy has generated several turnovers and made opponents uncomfortable trying to run their offense. Rookie Defining The Pace While the rules help, the execution relies on the speed and conditioning of rookie Zaccharie Risacher. In 29.5 minutes per contest over six games, the 21-year-old averages 2.0 steals and 1.7 blocks. Victor Wembanyama alone tops the entire NBA in combined steals and blocks, with his 22 ranking second. The coaching staff trusts Risacher to make smart plays even when he takes big risks to clean up mistakes made by teammates. May noted that Risacher arrived at summer workouts in excellent shape and has maintained that level of fitness throughout the season. He can play five hard minutes and sit on the bench without being out of breath. “He’s got great instincts, his motor, his conditioning. He came in this summer, the first day he came for workouts, he was in really good physical condition. So that’s a big part of it,” May said, according to Yardbarker . The coach believes this endurance comes from both genetics and the work Risacher put in during the offseason. “I’m sure DNA is a percentage of it, but also his offseason work,” May said. “I think he’s just a guy that never gets out of shape, so he’s never fighting to get back in.” Winning The Grind On Friday night, Dallas secured a win over the Houston Rockets thanks to this defensive identity in a game decided at the end. The lead changed hands nine times, and the Mavericks had to match the physical intensity of their rivals to survive. After missing time with a thumb injury, Caleb Martin saw the entire fourth quarter during his second game back. May praised the team’s ability to handle the rough play. He noted that while some teams struggle to match intensity when shots aren’t falling, Dallas has shown they can stay tough. item.title: From nightmare debut season to Everton hero - Barry's revival
item.description: [Getty Images] Last season Thierno Barry scored eight goals in 41 appearances. This season it's taken him just 12 games to match that tally. On Monday night Barry scored against Newcastle for the second time in five days as his side earned a deserved win at St James' Park in the Premier League. Only Erling Haaland (13) has scored more goals among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Barry (eight). The 24-year-old is on his best run of form since joining the club from Villarreal last summer and, as Everton's only recognised senior striker following Beto's transfer to Fiorentina, is currently indispensable to the Toffees. By scoring once again Barry highlighted why Everton paid £27m for a striker who grew up watching Wayne Rooney and Romelu Lukaku score for the Toffees. The Frenchman had a rough start to life on Merseyside, having just one shot across his first 16 Everton games, and last month posted a video of himself breaking down during a private training session last season. That moment was contrasted by his celebration on Monday night, which started with a knee slide and ended with dance moves. "I was working a lot during the summer and now we can see the result," Barry told Sky Sports. "The season is long but I'm happy to help the team with my goals. "I want to enjoy more than last season and I enjoyed my celebration so I am happy." It was a controversial strike though with Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle telling BBC Sport there was "a clear foul on Fabian Schar" in the build-up. Who produced the kind of performance Moyes loves? - player ratings Barry cements himself as Everton's main man In the Premier League Barry leads the way for being involved in the highest proportion of his team's big chances. Before Monday's match, Everton had recorded 24 big chances, and Barry had been involved in 15 of them (62.5%). The striker has often been criticised for being wasteful in front of goal. In Monday's match, for instance, he latched on to Jarrad Branthwaite's flick-on but, when through on goal, made a poor connection with the ball and scuffed his shot. His goal - a tap-in from two yards - was very difficult not to convert, with the opportunity having had an incredibly high xG of 0.995. "We know Barry misses chances, but we also know this season he keeps going and he scores goals," former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher told Sky Sports. His manager David Moyes added: "We're thrilled he's getting the goals because you need your centre-forward to score. He has missed a few but thankfully tonight he was on the spot to get the goal." item.title: Detroit Tigers bring back Drew Anderson, let Kenley Jansen walk
item.description: The Detroit Tigers made a flurry of moves on Monday, Nov. 2, offering some clues about the direction they are headed. The big news: Tigers right-hander Drew Anderson is staying, while veteran closer Kenley Jansen is leaving. The Tigers exercised their 2027 club option for Anderson, a swingman signed after multiple seasons in Asia who proved effective after moving from the bullpen to a starting role, and declined their club option for Jansen, who struggled in 2026 with a 3.20 ERA, a 4-6 record and earned just 22 saves, his lowest total since 2020. He finished the season with 498 career saves, but his quest to become the third pitcher in MLB history with 500 saves will have to continue somewhere else. In addition, the Tigers announced that they signed right-handed reliever Jacob Waguespack to a one-year, $1.3 million major-league contract for the 2027 season. The deal also includes performance bonuses that could bring the total value to $1.5 million: $25,000 for reaching both 45 innings and 50 innings pitched and $50,000 for reaching 55, 60 and 65 innings. JEFF SEIDEL: Tigers top prospect Zyhir Hope showing growth at Arizona Fall League The Tigers also activated seven players off of the 60-day injured list: OF Kerry Carpenter, OF Parker Meadows, RHP Reese Olson, OF Wenceel Pérez, INF Trey Sweeney, RHP Will Vest and OF Matt Vierling. Carpenter had a heel injury that became plantar fasciitis, costing him the final two months, while Meadows missed nearly all of the season after an outfield collision with Riley Greene in Minneapolis in early April. To make room on the 40-man roster, left-hnder Bailey Horn and right-hander Sawyer Gipson-Long have been placed on unconditional release waivers; outfielder Corey Julks has been outrighted off the 40-man roster and is now a free agent; and right-hander Yilber Díaz has been designated for assignment. Their offensive coordinator, Declan Doyle, ran the same system with the Bears last season. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio proposed a trade on Sunday night that would see the Ravens send a draft pick to the Chicago Bears for backup quarterback Tyson Bagent, who worked with Doyle in Chicago. “There is that familiarity there with Doyle and Tyson Bagent,” Florio said. “But that trade would be really hard to pull off at this point.” Bagent is a 26-year-old who signed a two-year, $10 million deal in 2025. He started two games this season when Caleb Williams was out, but his stats were rough with three interceptions and no touchdowns in three games. Despite the poor numbers, Doyle praised him last season, calling him “very businesslike” and noting he “sees the game pretty clearly.” The Ravens need someone who can step in immediately for their Thursday night game or after a mini-bye, and Bagent fits that specific need. Why Chicago Says No Even though Baltimore is desperate, the Bears have no intention of selling. LaCanfora added that the Bears have been rejecting any offers for Bagent through the summer, as there’s belief he’s a valuable backup in Ben Johnson’s offense. One NFL GM told LaCanfora that “Chicago doesn’t have to trade him. They like him … Wonder how hard they squeeze (Ravens GM Eric) DeCosta?” The Bears could ride out the rest of the season with Case Keenum as the backup and look to draft a younger QB later. After Huntley was injured, the Ravens gave undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano a chance, but he completed only 10 of his 21 passes for 91 yards with no touchdowns and one interception. That performance showed why Baltimore is panicked. If Chicago refuses to move Bagent, the Ravens might have to target Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett instead. The trade deadline is November 10, giving both teams a few days to see if a deal can be made.

item.description: The Arizona Cardinals found a way to win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and they needed to pull off something historic to do so. Behind the performances of backup quarterback Gardner Minshew II and running back Tyler Allgeier, the Cardinals thwarted the Cowboys for a 33-30 victory. Dallas had the lead until the final kick and was up by two touchdowns early in the fourth quarter. The Cowboys could have also lost in regulation, but a missed PAT from Arizona kicker Chad Ryland in the closing seconds of regulation led to overtime. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Makes History in Kansas City Chiefs’ Loss
item.description: Patrick Mahomes reached a notable career milestone Sunday, even as the Kansas City Chiefs surrendered a late lead in a 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. The quarterback recorded his 49th regular-season game with at least three touchdown passes during his first 10 NFL seasons, moving ahead of Peyton Manning’s 48. Mahomes completed 30 of 41 attempts for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions at Empower Field at Mile High. His performance helped the team build a 24-13 advantage, but the offense could not produce another score after Noah Gray’s four-yard touchdown catch late in the third quarter. The passing total marked his second 300-yard outing of the season. Oct 19, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) gets ready prior to a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images The milestone came on that connection with Gray, which capped an 11-play, 63-yard drive and gave the team an 11-point lead. Mahomes had already thrown touchdown passes to Rashee Rice and rookie Emmett Johnson, whose 73-yard reception in the second quarter marked the longest scoring play of the afternoon. Johnson finished with five catches for 128 yards. Denver began its comeback in the fourth quarter, when Bo Nix connected with Nate Adkins for a two-yard touchdown and then found Jaylen Waddle for a two-point conversion. After kicker Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, the Broncos moved quickly, with rookie Jonah Coleman gaining 51 yards on a reception before scoring on a five-yard run to put Denver ahead 28-24 with 1:56 remaining. The sequence flipped the lead after the visitors had controlled much of the game. Kansas City Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes Achieves Historic Record in Loss to Denver Broncos Dec 14, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) looks to pass against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Kenneth Walker was stopped short on third down, and after a false start pushed the offense back, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes on fourth-and-goal to end the game and preserve the Broncos’ victory. The defense held firm despite allowing 399 total yards. The result dropped the team to 5-2 and moved Denver to 6-2, giving the Broncos the AFC West lead. The record-setting total added another milestone to Mahomes ‘ early career, but the team will have to address its late-game execution after losing two consecutive contests. Probably the most surprising part of the Tigers decisions today was the fact that they reinstated seven of eight players from the 60-day injured list. Some of the players they kept still aren’t going to make it through the offseason, as the Tigers 40-man roster now stands full at 40 players. item.title: Robert Griffin III says he wants to be Baylor's next football coach
item.description: Former Heisman winner Robert Griffin III confirms talks with Baylor about its head coaching vacancy following Dave Aranda's firing. (EDWARD A. ORNELAS/SAN ANTONIO EXPRESS-NEWS) Former Baylor quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III wants to return to his alma mater, this time as its head football coach. Griffin, who won the Heisman Trophy in 2011, confirmed he has spoken with Baylor officials about the opening after the school fired Dave Aranda on Sunday, according to Front Office Sports . "If I was making all the decisions, the decision would have already been made, right?" Griffin told Front Office Sports Tonight. "But that's not the process, and I'm looking forward to going through that process with Baylor University to have real, concrete conversations." He emphasized leadership, recruiting and building a winning culture. "The coaching in college is no longer about who calls plays," Griffin said. "It's about being a CEO and being able to manage not only the pressure, but also building a culture of winning." Griffin also pointed to his Texas roots, recruiting connections and familiarity with Baylor's Christian mission as qualifications for the position. Baylor fired Aranda after seven seasons and a 40-40 record, including one bowl victory. Griffin, who has a statue outside Baylor's McLane Stadium, said he believes he has the support and leadership skills to turn the program around. item.title: Giants Miss Chance To Land Daron Payne Before Injury
item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The New York Giants had a real shot to fix their defensive line, but a broken foot ended the deal before it could happen. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that New York was actively talking about trading for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne before the injury struck. “He was the subject of trade talks,” Rapoport said. The timing is brutal for a team sitting at 4-2-1 in the NFC East. Payne fractured his foot during Friday’s practice and will miss the rest of the season. This leaves the Giants with the same roster problems they faced last week. Trade Talks That Never Happened The Giants were looking for help inside the defensive line after trading Dexter Lawrence earlier this year. They have leaned on veterans like D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris, but the team wanted more. Rapoport noted that a deal between division rivals was on the table. “In fact, we’re told the Giants had interest in Daron Payne — a possible intra-division trade. We will never know whether or not that was actually going to happen,” Rapoport said. The Commanders were ready to move Payne before the November 10 deadline since he is in the final year of his contract. Now that window is shut. The Giants have to find another way to get better. Running Back Room Shakes Up While the defense lost a chance at Payne, the offense lost a key piece on the ground. Tyrone Tracy Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury that occurred during the overtime win against Houston on Sunday. GM Joe Schoen addressed the media during the bye week and offered some hope. “This won’t be something that’s going to be long-term — fortunately,” he said. Tracy had three touchdowns in his last two games and is now out while the team looks for answers. Gregory Desrosiers was signed from the Chargers’ practice squad to fill the hole. The running back room was already in the spotlight after the Saints loss. After all four backs dressed for that game, Coach John Harbaugh stated that someone needed to “take the bull by the horns” The Road Ahead in the East The Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, but the path is getting harder. The Cowboys dropped to 3-5 after losing to the Cardinals in overtime on Sunday. The Eagles fell to 2-6 after a 27-10 loss to Washington. New York faces a tough schedule with two division games coming up. On Sunday, November 8, at 1 p.m. ET, they travel to Philadelphia, with a Thursday night home game against Washington following. The coaching staff knows what is coming. Harbaugh stated the coaching staff will focus on two games during the bye week, adding that his record stands at 15-3 in contests right after the bye. The team has the lead, but they cannot afford to slip up against a team like the Eagles or the Commanders. The loss of Payne and Tracy makes the job much harder.

item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The 2026 Gold Glove awards landed on Sunday with a clear message for the rest of the league: the Atlanta Braves are built on grit. Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubón did not just make the list; they own it. Olson secured his fourth career award, while Dubón added his third to a resume that already includes wins in 2023 and 2025. This isn’t luck. It is a system that values range and hands over raw power. While the Boston Red Sox and Arizona Diamondbacks tied for the most winners with three each, the Braves made sure their stars stood out in the crowd. According to ESPN , Olson previously won the honor in 2018, 2019, and 2025, showing a consistency that few first basemen can match. The Red Sox got hype for Wilyer Abreu, who took his third straight title, and Ceddanne Rafaela, who won for the second year running. But in Atlanta, we know that one or two elite defenders can change the entire complexion of a playoff series. Dubón Is The Unsung Hero Mauricio Dubón earned his third Gold Glove, underscoring his defensive value. He covers ground that most utility men can only dream of. Per Fox Sports , the utility category uses a specific Society for American Baseball Research defensive index to calculate the winners. This means Dubón didn’t just look good on tape; the numbers backed him up too. The 2021 title run was built on players who could move around the diamond without losing a step. Dubón fits that mold perfectly. He plays multiple spots, makes the tough plays, and keeps the defense stable when the lineup gets shaky. It is a quiet skill, but it wins games. The Voting Process Has Changed Winning these awards is harder now than it was a decade ago. Since 2013, the voting has mixed the eyes of managers and coaches with hard data from the SABR defensive index. That data makes up about 25% of the total vote, according to reports from Fox Sports. This shift stops voters from just picking the guy with the best highlight reel. While managers and a maximum of six coaches per team submit the votes, they are prohibited from selecting players from their own club. This rule forces them to look at the league as a whole. It prevents bias and forces a true comparison of skill. When a player like Olson or Dubón wins under these rules, it means they are truly the best in the game. No flukes. No home-field advantage in the voting booth. The money attached to these wins is small, but the prestige is huge. Walker earned a $75,000 bonus for his win, while Turang took home $25,000. The Braves have now secured multiple awards in a season where the competition was fierce. That is the standard we set. The 2026 Gold Gloves were awarded in Atlanta.
